Director Taika Waititi Responds to Negative Reviews for 'Klara and the Sun'

Director Taika Waititi has publicly addressed negative critical reception surrounding his latest film, *Klara and the Sun*, following its recent theatrical release.

Social Media Response

Writing on Instagram, Waititi shared the film's promotional poster alongside a comparison of its ratings on Rotten Tomatoes. The posted image indicated a notable difference between audience reception and critic evaluations, showing a higher audience approval rating compared to a lower score from professional reviewers.

In his accompanying caption, the filmmaker stated that he avoids reading reviews directed at his work. He also shared critical remarks aimed at reviewers, comparing audience perspectives with critical evaluations.

Box Office Performance

*Klara and the Sun* debuted in North American theaters across 880 locations. Reports indicate the feature earned an estimated opening weekend gross in domestic markets and has accumulated additional earnings globally since its release.

Film Overview and Themes

Based on Kazuo Ishiguro’s 2021 dystopian novel of the same title, the movie explores a future where artificial intelligence companions exist. The narrative centers on an obsolete android attempting to connect with a young, ailing owner named Josie.

  • Cast Members: The film stars Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams.
  • Central Themes: Artificial intelligence, companionship, and human connection.

During a prior interview at the New York premiere, Waititi discussed the real-world implications of artificial intelligence. He expressed the view that while the technology may see increased integration in the entertainment industry, it should function as a human-directed tool rather than a replacement for creative personnel.

How to Verify

Audiences and interested viewers can verify box office figures through industry tracking publications like *The Hollywood Reporter* or check current aggregator scores directly on Rotten Tomatoes.
